source: You decided to tell the visitor that you and Jorge were indispensable experts with the Artifact.
You decided to tell the visitor that you and Jorge were indispensable experts with the Artifact.
You decided to try convincing the visitor that the Artifact was too dangerous.
You changed your mind, deciding to tell the visitor the Artifact was extremely dangerous.
You changed your mind, deciding to tell the visitor the Artifact had died.
You changed your mind, deciding to tell the visitor that you and Jorge were indispensable.
Next
We'll probably get a raise, right?
It's going to be so nice finally having a home-cooked meal. Fresh vegetables. Home-made sauce...
We're going to be on a whole new level once we come back. We'll never have to worry about funding again.
I don't know.
"Jorgeli". Maybe that's what we'll call it. "A Jorgelian Life form."
Anything you want to do out here before they bring us back?
It'll be great to see your kids again, huh?
Alright. Go get everything in order. I'll be here keeping the fire going if you need me.
Will do, thanks Jorge.
Spoken like a true scientist. Always a bigger discovery to be found. A way to remedy what feels like an impossible situation.
What are you driving at?
Anyway, what are you going to miss most?
So you're saying there's still hope?
Yes.
But a chance at despair as well.
Touché.
What are you going to miss most, Jorge?
I'd...I'd like a few minutes to gather my thoughts. Besides, someone needs to make sure the fire goes out.
Gotcha.
[Nod]
Goodnight, Eli.
Goodnight, Jorge.
Okay, sure. But we know that. You believe there's still some hope?
There's a sliver.
There's always hope.

Yeah...I can see it. Then they'd have to bring us back to lead the research. Or at least do some consulting. That'd give us some time to figure out something more permanent. But we'd really have to sell it.
How?
Any suggestions on how we do that?

Okay...That could buy us some time and allow our research out here to continue. I could have sworn it was dead when we had it in a pacified state, so it's definitely doable. But we're really going to have to sell it.
What do you mean?
Any suggestions on how we do that?
Can't wait to sleep in a proper bed. With pillows. A duvet...
Anything you want to do out here before they bring us back?
I might actually miss this place. There's a sense of calm out here. Quiet.
Hmm. Yeah. That might work. Then they'd need us to come back with them to keep it under control. Could buy us some time and maybe a bit of clout. We'll have to be convincing, though.
I don't see any other option. Let's do it.
I'm sure we can figure it out.
Well, first we'd have to figure out a way back that doesn't require a body-bag. You got anything?
Maybe.
Nope.
Well, we kind of are. What did you do when you found out about this assignment. Did you try to fight it?
No, I was just grateful they were still keeping me around after my little stunt.
What could I have done?

There's a good chance our visitor is going to comb through all our research to make sure we're telling the truth about the Artifact being dead. Make sure that everything on-site lines up with that story. Our journals, research, even the Artifact itself. We can't leave anything to chance.
Gotcha. Thanks, Jorge.
Gotcha.
[Nod]

There's a good chance our visitor is going to comb through everything on site to make sure we really know our stuff. Make sure that everything on-site lines up with that story. Our journals, research, even the Artifact itself. We can't leave anything to chance.
Gotcha. Thanks, Jorge.

Whoever's coming is probably going to comb through the entire site to make sure we're telling the truth about how dangerous this thing is. Make sure that everything on-site lines up with that. Our journals, research, even the Artifact itself. We can't leave anything to chance.
Gotcha. Thanks, Jorge.
That works. Now go out there and make sure everything on site sells the idea that the Artifact is as dangerous as possible. Research, journals, even the Artifact itself. Got it?
Got it.
Yeah, yeah.
Fine by me. Now go out there and make sure everything on site sells the idea that the Artifact's dead and we have the ability to find a new one. Research, journals, even the Artifact itself. Got it?
Got it.
Yeah, yeah...
Fine by me. Now go out there and make us look like geniuses. Everything on site should sell the idea that we really know our shit. Research, journals, even the Artifact itself. Got it?
Got it.
Yeah, yeah...
Right...
It'll be great to see your kids again, huh?
Anything you want to do out here before they bring us back?
I might actually miss this place. There's a sense of calm out here. Quiet.
Let's talk about something more positive, then. What do you think you're going to miss the most?
My parents.
The work.
The promise of tomorrow.
(CYNIC) How is making me think about the things I love that I'll never see again a more "positive" line of discussion?
Let me ask you something, Eli: Why do you suppose you were assigned to this detail?
Because it's my job.
My supervisors wanted me to get more field experience.
Probably because I don't have a family yet. No attachments.
You're giving me a weird look.
You're just...really calm.
This is just my face.
Yeah. Well, stop pointing it at mine.
Okay.
...I can't change my face.
Whatever's about to happen...it's out of my hands. Might as well enjoy what's left.
I'll try.
You're bumming me out, Jorge.
They really are. Ugh, I'm going to miss them so much. I should have just quit. I knew exactly what this job was going to be, but I let them tell me otherwise.
You'll see them again. I'm going to see to it.
I wish I had known.
The quiet or the city?
The quiet.
Both.
Well, if things go the way I expect, we'll be in for a lot more quiet from here on out.
Good.
And if you're wrong?
Nothing but cheers and applause from our friends in the scientific community. I can see the articles now: "First team to survive the ravenous Wastes: How did they ever survive?"
I don't want to think about it.
translation: Я не хочу об этом думать.

source: No need to be sarcastic.
(IDEALIST) It's not out of the realm of possibility.
Uh-huh.
Okay, what's up? You're not even listening to me.
Is something wrong?
Earth to Jorge...
Are you serious? That's when you need them the most!
It's my fault.
They have their own legacies to protect.
Gotcha.
[Nod]
Huh. Well, if the worst happens, at least they'll be able to say "he died doing what he loved."
I hope it wasn't in vain.
I was hoping you might put that theoretical background to use. Come up with some sort of plan.
I might have something...
I'm drawing a blank.
Not right now. Let's talk about you. What are you going to miss most?
Anything's possible, Eli. But that doesn't make it plausible.
I just want to enjoy my last few hours, Jorge.
[Sigh deeply]
Well, keep drawing. Eventually some ink will trickle out.
You're right! I got this.
I'll give it a shot.
Is that because the future is bright, or because the present is dark?
(IDEALIST) The future is bright.
(REALIST) The present determines the future. We're not completely powerless.
(CYNIC) Our bosses are about to kill us, Jorge. What do you think?
No idea. But if they're going to be bringing something back from outside the wall, it's probably someone at the top. Or above it.
We're not high level and they sent us.
Which is what we are now. After this discovery, I mean.
Yes, but nobody said we're coming back.
What are you talking about?
They didn't say we weren't.
Well, obviously they're going to bring us back too.
Good memories are good memories, Eli. Just because they aren't going to repeat themselves doesn't make them worthless.
What are you going to miss most?
Do you...do you follow the Scripture, Eli?
(CYNIC) You mean that superstitious nonsense they use to control us?
(REALIST) I don't follow anything I can't see.
(IDEALIST) No, but I appreciate the value it brings to others. Even if I don't understand it.
Do you?
No, Jorge. I follow science.
That's in the early days, though. Before the outside became the Wastes. And it's just a story.
Then we're the first.
'A story'? I thought you were a believer.

Family, probably. My mom...my sister...my nephews. I'm really going to miss them. After my last promotion, I was able to move them into a nice little high-rise in Granville. Even got an extra bedroom so I can stay over whenever I'm able to get away from work. Which is rare, but when I can? Man... it's the world.
You cover their rent?
How old are your nephews?
They're eight and nine, but the way they stick together you'd swear that they're twins. Matteo and Seb. Total troublemakers. My mother calls them "The Scamps".
You ever think of having kids of your own?
What kind of trouble do they get themselves into?
Nah, I got my hands full with the scamps. Plus, I've never had much luck in relationships.
Me either.
How come?
Pranks, mostly. They've gotten really into hard-boiled eggs lately.
What, like, eating them?
Like, collecting them?

I wish. No, they've been boiling them, peeling the shell off and chucking them like snowballs. They keep throwing them at the windows of the neighbouring high rise to wake them up in the middle of the night and it started a geezer infestation on the street below.
That's actually kind of cool.
Disgusting.
It's not a big deal. Granville's actually a lot cheaper than Science City. I pay more for my shitty studio apartment than I do for all four of their bedrooms.
Couldn't you just live there and commute to Science City?
Have you ever thought of starting your own family?

I used to when I was younger, but it got too hard.  Eight hour turnarounds and unreliable transit really took its toll. Now I just visit whenever I can. Or at least, I did. Ugh, I should have quit when I had the chance.
You'll see them again, Eli. I'll see to it.
Or at least warned me about what I was about to step into.

Thankfully, no. That would be so pungent. They've been boiling the eggs, peeling the shells off and chucking them like snowballs. They keep throwing them at the windows of the neighbouring high rise to wake them up in the middle of the night and it started a geezer infestation on the street below.
That's actually kind of cool.
Disgusting.
I think so too! But don't tell their mother that. I think it's actually impressive they found a way to throw things at windows without breaking the glass. Clever little scamps...
When did you last see them?
They sound cool.
No.
Okay, what's up? You're not even listening to me.
Is something wrong?
Earth to Jorge...
Yeah, it's not great. I am a little impressed that they found a way to throw things at windows without breaking the glass. Clever little scamps...
When did you last see them?
They sound cool.
Goodnight, Eli.
Night, Jorge.
Night, Jorge.
Sorry, I'm just...I guess it's all starting to get to me.
I don't want to think about that right now.
It's possible nothing's going to happen to us.
What are you going to miss the most?
The work.
The promise of tomorrow.

Ah, yes. A stress like that'll make you ignore the reddest of flags. I actually threatened to quit, but they made it clear that doing so would cost me my retirement plan, so I decided to play the optimist.
Maybe that's still possible.
Well, aren't we a couple of idiots?
Oh, yeah! I forgot they used to be bigheads at Science City. Wait...how come they never warned you about this assignment?
We're not very close. I only really see them on holidays.
I never talk work with them.
I actually threatened to quit, but they made it clear that doing so would cost me my retirement plan, so I decided to ignore the obvious and hope for the best.
That might still be possible.
Well, aren't we a couple of idiots?
Okay, what's up? You're not even listening to me.
Is something wrong, Jorge?
Earth to Jorge...
Nature of the job, I guess. The work's too busy to allow you to build a life and too important to give up.
My parents made it work. Kind of.
I wish I could give it up.
Well, sure. The achievements of two people will almost always beat one. Unless we actually manage to find a way back through that wall.
Actually, I might have a plan for that...
What are you suggesting?
You're their son, Eli. You are their legacy.
I wish they would see it that way.
Nah, I'm just a threat to the one they already built.
No. Fuck that. This is exactly the kind of craven shit that lets HQ do whatever sociopathic shit they want — no questions asked. We need to do something. We can't let them win.
What are you suggesting?
Smells good, doesn't it? Pretty sure it's Maple.
I love it.
[sniff it in]
Then why are you going to miss them?
They're all I have.
I dunno. I guess I needed to give some kind of an answer.
Okay, what's your answer then? What are you going to miss?
Why didn't you?
Couldn't think of anything better.
I didn't want to disappoint my parents.
Shit, Eli. That's just...that's just too fucking sad. I just can't let you go out on a note like that. It's just not right.
What are you suggesting?
Me? I'm not suggesting anything. But if some bigshot PhD with a theoretical background were to come up with a cunning plan, I would probably have no choice but to follow.
Let me see what I can come up with...
I might have something.
Oh, yeah! I forgot they used to be bigheads at Science City. Wait...how come they never warned you about this assignment?
I never talk work with them.
They stopped talking to me after I pulled that stunt that landed me here.
As do I. I never thought the two to be mutually exclusive. But now I'm not so sure. Are you...are you familiar with the story of the Sighted Skeptic?
Oh no. Are you going to try to convert me?
Can't say that I have. Enlighten me.
No, but I have the feeling you're going to tell me...
It was a simple "yes" or "no" question, Eli. Not an invitation to soapbox. Though I'm starting to wonder if you might be right. Are...are you familiar with the story of the Sighted Skeptic?
Oh no. You're not going to try to convert me, are you?
Can't say that I have. What's it about?
No, but I have the feeling you're going to tell me...
You're still up? Go get some sleep, man! I'll take care of the fire.
Will do.
Never heard anything like this in city. You know, we might be the only people alive who know what real quiet sounds like.
I like it.
I'm going to miss it.

I can appreciate that. Growing up in the West End, it was always comforting to believe that, no matter how bad things would get, the Shepherd was watching over us. I'm beginning to think that might not be the case anymore. Are...are you familiar with the story of the Sighted Skeptic?
Oh no. Are you going to try to convert me?
Can't say that I have. What's it about?
No, but I have the feeling you're going to tell me...
That's very refreshing to hear, Eli. Most of our colleagues in Science City aren't as...open-minded about the Shepherd's teachings. Are you familiar with the story of the Sighted Skeptic?
Oh no. Are you going to try to convert me?
Can't say that I have. What's it about?
No, but I have the feeling you're going to tell me...

I did. All my life. Growing up in the West End, it was always comfort knowing that, no matter how bad things got, the Shepherd was always out there, watching over me. Ready to intervene, if necessary. But now? I don't... Are you familiar with the story of the Sighted Skeptic?
Oh no. Are you going to try to convert me?
Can't say that I have. Enlighten me.
No, but I have the feeling you're going to tell me...
Not at all. It's just...it's a story that's been on my mind ever since we passed The Wall. Feels particularly relevent to the... predicament we find ourselves in.
What predicament? Being on the verge of wild success?
What's it about?

Years ago, long before the creation of The Wall, the Shepherd would scour the wasteland, guiding lost followers through the mountains towards the promised land. The path was treacherous and the elevation so high that each follower would inevitably become blinded by the sun, forcing them to rely entirely on His voice for guidance.
(REALIST) Why didn't the Shepherd also lose his sight?
(CYNIC) Why wouldn't the Shepherd just give them sunglasses?
Hmm.
[Nod]
(IDEALIST) Probably just temporary blindness, right?
Ah, the faith of the faithless really is something to behold. You really don't see it, do you?
Just get to the point, man.
See what?
Not you. Us. The minute we went outside the wall, we became a threat to the rest of the flock. Because of what we've seen.
I think we're more like the Shepherd, honestly. We've both gone beyond the wall and come back.
How do you figure?
Sorry. I just...it's a story that's been on my mind ever since we passed the Wall. I think it's particularly relevent to the... predicament we find ourselves in.
Go on...
What predicament? Being on the verge of wild success?
Because he's the Shepherd.
Seems awfully convenient.
That makes him impervious to UV rays?
How's the prep coming?
I think everything's ready.
What exactly should I be doing again?
I think we should go with a different approach.
Still working on it.
Yes.
Alright, go on.
Fair enough.
I don't know. I suppose because they'd melt.
If the heat is melting plastic, they would surely die of heatstroke as well.
Makes sense. Keep going.
Alright, I made up the thing about melting. Maybe the Shepherd just didn't want to lug hundreds of pairs of sunglasses with him on top of leading people to the promised land.
He could have just told them to shield their eyes when they got close.
Seems kind of worth it to prevent blindness.
Right. I wouldn't either.
Once they reached the City, the Shepherd promised to guide them towards the ocean, where their sight would be restored by the healing waters of The Great Blue.
(CYNIC) Seems unlikely.
Convenient.
Nice.
[Nod]
Can you stop focusing on this? The blindness is only temporary. Once they get to the City, they regain it by washing themselves in The Great Blue. Now, will you please stop interrupting me?
I'm just curious.
[Shrug]
Well...much like Micah, we have now seen things that we weren't supposed to see. Which makes us a liability.
You're talking about the Artifact.
You're talking about leaving the city.
Exactly. After reaching the City, the Shepherd promised to guide them towards the ocean, where their sight would be restored by the cool waters of The Great Blue.
Of course.
Nice.
It's...not to be taken literally. It's more of a parable. A lesson. About learning things that betray the common good.
What's that have to do with us?
Go on.
One year, a follower named Micah was so afraid of losing his sight—even temporarily—that he covered his eyes with bandages in advance to protect them from the sun’s rays.
Smart man.
I like Micah.
[Nod]

Once the flock descended from the highest point of the mountain, Micah began to remove his bandages. Finally able to see, Micah became acutely aware of all the dangers that surrounded them. He started screaming words of warnings to his fellow travelers, causing them to doubt the Shepherd's calm directives, leading some of them to misstep and tumble down the mountain towards their deaths.
[Shake head sadly]
What an asshole.
[Nod]
You sure?
Yes.
Actually, now that you mention it... Give me a second.

This chaos caused Micah’s warnings to become even louder, even more hysterical. Even more of followers began to lose their footing and began to fall! Desperate to stop this carnage, the Shepherd marched towards Micah and struck him with his staff until he fell unconscious.
Hmm.
Badass.
That's what I'd do too.

With Micah silenced, the followers were soon able to continue along the path, following the Shepherd's calm and trusted voice towards the City where their sights were soon restored and the rest of their days were spent in health and prosperity.
What happened to Micah?
Good for them.
Sweet.
It's believed that Micah remains at the top of that mountain to this very day, where he screams into the void, too paralyzed by fear to move forward.
So, let me guess. I'm supposed to be Micah?
Okay. But what's your point?
Wouldn't Micah be dead by now?
What?
Nothing.
I didn't say anything.

And what, faked their deaths? If that's true, where are they? No, there's something deeper going on here. I think...I think they're not being allowed to come back. Because of what they know. And what we know.
What do we know?
I think you've been out in the sun too long.
How many people can you name who have returned to the city after leaving it?
I can't. We'd be the first.
The Shepherd.
None by name. I've heard rumours, though.
All those people in the story.

That's what I'm thinking. This was supposed to be a suicide mission. Everything we've been told about the world beyond the wall says that. And yet HQ is completely unphased by the fact that we've been out here six months. They've even given us enough provisions to last a year. It doesn't add up.
Maybe they're just...optimistic.
They just want us to be prepared.
What reason would they have to eliminate us? We don't know anything.
Not exactly, though that may be part of it. I'm talking about leaving the city. That we know what it's actually like out here.
How does that make us a liability?
But there's nothing out here. I mean, besides the Artifact.
We haven't come back yet. And that's my point. How many people can you name who've returned from beyond the wall?
We'd be the first.
The, uh...the Shepherd.
I've heard rumours of others.

I did. I mean...I do. It's just... The scripture also claims that the outside world is completely unliveable. That's the core tenent of Scripture. Even the strongest and most well-equipped among us would perish within days, if not hours. We've been here six months, Eli. There's no danger. Which means there must be another reason why no one has come back.
Someone's stopping them. Or something.
Maybe they like it better out here.
Good. Then it's just a matter of time. Go get some rest. We'll need to be at our sharpest when this visitor arrives.
Will do.
You coming?
And why do you suppose that is? Why has no one else ever come back from beyond the wall?
Because we're better than them. We braved the elements.
Because it's dangerous. They've all fallen to the elements.

I got old, Eli. Not as glamorous a reason as yours, but with my retirement coming up and I suppose the number crunchers realized a detail like this would save them on pension. Wouldn't be the first. And definitely not the last.
Sounds about right.
Good old HQ. Always looking after the bottom line.
Because of what we know.
I think you've been out in the sun for way too long.
What do we know?

Did we? Because outside of that one incident with the Artifact, this expedition has been fairly routine. No real threats, no big dangers. Just the hot hot sun and our clashing personalities. So, if it's not the elements killing these other teams, what is?
HQ.
You tell me.
Maybe they liked it out here and decided to stay?
The Shepherd isn't a person. He's the Shepherd. And you don't even believe he exists.
Fine. Just us, then.
You believe in him, though.
In a way. If you could leave the City and start your own thing, wouldn't you?
No. I love the City.
The City's all there is.
Only rumours. In all my time working in Science City, I've heard of at least a dozen expeditions similar to ours. None of them have returned. Do you know why?
Because they weren't as trained as us. We braved the elements.
Because it's dangerous out here.

Whoever is coming here is going to go through this site with a fine tooth comb to make sure our story checks out. We'll need to make sure all our materials sell the idea that we're experts on the Artifact.
I'm on it.
How do we do that?

Really? Where's the danger? The only real hazard we've encountered so far is that Artifact. And we had to work very fucking hard to find that. Outside of that, everything's been fine. Peaceful, even. I honestly feel safer here than I did back in the city. Which begs the question: why hasn't anyone ever come back from the place?
They're not allowed.
You tell me.
Maybe they like it better out here.

That's only because you were born in Science City - gifted child to gifted parents, brought up in a block where the Apes actually look after you. You never had to struggle. You don't really know how bad most of us have it.
Don't condescend to me, man. You live in Science City too.
Hey, I earned my place.
Mmm.
Do they still name discoveries after the people who found them?
As soon as we get back, let's go to dinner. Somewhere fancy. My treat.
We've got it made now! No more red tape. No more having to suck up to committees.

This is just a theory, but here's what I'm thinking: Back in the city, we're penned in. Cornered. Easy to control. The Apes own all the land so we have to do whatever they want just to borrow a sliver for our families to sleep in. Scarcity is key, Eli. If the people knew there was a world outside the City—a safe, dusty, perfectly normal world with space enough for all of us—the entire system would COLLAPSE.
So what, this is all about control? Real estate?
They're going to bring us back. They didn't mention it because it's obvious.
Really, Jorge? Conspiracy theories?
Or maybe, the real danger isn't out here. Maybe it's on it's way.
So they're going to kill us? Why?
You mean whoever's coming from HQ.
Alright. Go get everything in order. I'll be here keeping the fire going if you need me.
Later, Jorge.

You need to stop deluding yourself, Eli. No team has ever come back from behind the Wall. We're on a suicide mission. For an outsider like me, this was always going to be the retirement plan. That's just how Science City works. But you're still young. Connected. You must have upset some really powerful people to get assigned a detail like this. So what happened?
(CYNIC) My team that was working with radiation waves to "persuade" test subjects to adopt more "desirable" behaviours. I could see where it was heading and leaked some info to the press.
(IDEALIST) Well... I didn't think they found out, but I may have helped leak the formula of a lifesaving medication to our competitors to drive prices down.
(REALIST) I may have mentioned that a new drug's side effects outweighed its benefits. To the CEO. At an investor meeting.
Now I'm not so sure.
About time you came to your senses.
Maybe the Shepard is protecting us. Or maybe it's a test of your faith.

You're the reason they shut down the mind control project? Wow. They were just about to move to public testing, too. I'm impressed, Eli. Here I was, thinking you were just some stuck-up failson. But it turns out you're a hero this whole time.
Can't I be both?
Most people would have done it. I was just in the right place at the right time.
You're the reason Pylanta™ went generic?  That's...that's amazing, Eli! And here I was, thinking you were just some stuck-up failson. But it turns out you were a hero this whole time.
Can't I be both?
It needed to be done. People were dying.

Shepherd's staff! You're the reason they pulled the funding on Lygoti™? I heard that instead of curing depression, it just caused so much abdominal pain test subjects would beg the doctors to save their lives and they figured they could market it as "restoring the will to live".
That's exactly what happened.
It also made patients confuse their dreams with reality. And not in a fun way.
Radio says they're on their way. Should be less than twelve hours, now.
Who's this 'they'?
About time. Six months is way too much.
Making this discovery and surviving the Wastes. We're going to be in history books, Jorge!
Easy, Eli. All they said is that they'd be collecting the Artifact. No word about what they're doing with us.
What else are they going to do? Without the Artifact our work here is done.
Why would they? No need to state the obvious.
Don't be such a pessimist. We're going home!
Night, Jorge.
Then why haven't they told us that?
I don't know.
Maybe our visitor will.
Nice and simple. I can get behind that.
[Listen to the crackling of the wood]
[Enjoy the smell of the fire]
[Study Jorge's expression]

Night before we shipped out. Started tearing up right as I said my goodbyes. Kids had no idea why. You should have seen their faces! Seb even asked if he did something wrong... I should have just quit. I knew exactly what this was going to be.
You'll see them again. I'm going to make sure of it.
Should have warned me.

So, what? You think we just happened to "luck out"? That for six entire months we managed to avoid ALL the countless threats that we're led to believe exist out here. How did that happen, Eli? And don't just say it's because we're good at our jobs.
We are good at our jobs. At least I am, anyway.
I thought you were a man of faith.
I worked hard to get where I am. They "allowed" me to move into Science City. So for a very short while, yes - I "lived" in Science City. Past tense.
They're going to bring us back. It's going to be a big deal.
By that logic, so did I.
I kinda figured your parents would have warned you. Weren't they also bigheads at Science City?
I never talk about work with them.
They stopped talking to me after I pulled that stunt that landed me here.
It's actually worth a lot back in the city. Only used for high-end furniture because it's so rare. If folks knew we were burning this for warmth, they'd call us crazy.
They'd also think we're crazy for being out here.
Let's smuggle some back.

I was. When I got assigned this detail, I actually looked forward to the dangers! I wanted to face them, because then it would have proved that I lived my life properly. That the Shepherd was real. That the stories they told us were true.
He could still be real, man.
That's messed up.
And now?
And no one to ask questions.
